chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Halal and the Haram, so he said: The Halal of Muhammad is Halal forever unto the Day of Judgment, and his Haram is Haram forever unto the Day of Judgment, there will be nothing other than it and nothing apart from it will come, and he said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: No one has innovated a Bid'a except that he has abandoned a Sunna by doing so.
ai.seo_question: What is the permanence of Halal and Haram in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the finality of the Prophet's (SAWW) legislative authority, affirming that his declarations of Halal and Haram are immutable until the Day of Judgment, a concept central to Shia Usul al-Fiqh regarding the cessation of revelation. It further connects this permanence to Imam Ali’s (AS) teaching that any religious innovation (Bid'a) inherently displaces an established Sunnah, highlighting the dialectic between preserving tradition and introducing novelty in Shia jurisprudence.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/-] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from Muhammad b. Isa b. Ubayd from Yunus from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about the Halal and the Haram so he said: the Halal of Muhammad is Halal forever unto the day of judgment and his Haram is Haram forever unto the day of judgment, there will be nothing other than it and nothing apart from it will come, and he said: Ali عليه السلام said: no one has innovated a Bid’a except that he has abandoned a Sunna (by doing so).
